text:
jess: hitting a weird redwoodctl auth issue on WSL2 — `redwoodctl login` opens the browser but nothing completes, CLI just hangs and eventually times out. anyone seen this?

adam: WSL can be funky with the browser redirect. try `redwoodctl login --browser=none` and paste the code flow.

jess: tried that, the CLI prints a URL and code but when I paste the code I get `error: invalid_verification_code` after a retry.

lisa: which redwoodctl version? and is your ~/.redwood/config.yaml present? sometimes profile creation races if config is empty.

jess: v0.12.1. my config exists but it only has a blank `profiles:` key. paste of logs: ```
$ redwoodctl login --browser=none
Open this URL in your browser: https://auth.redwood.ai/authorize?...
Enter verification code: ABCD-1234
Verifying...
error: invalid_verification_code
```

michael: repo note — we had a bug where the CLI would retry the verification endpoint twice with a stale nonce on WSL due to clock skew handling; that caused 400/401s. should be fixed in master (PR #2146).

jess: any short workaround until the release? can't get local serve running because it needs a profile token.

adam: workaround: use a hosted browser on your host (not WSL). from Windows/mac run the browser flow, then copy the token into WSL. steps: 1) on host run `redwoodctl login` complete in browser 2) cat ~/.redwood/config.yaml and copy the profile block 3) paste into WSL at ~/.redwood/config.yaml.

lisa: alternative: `redwoodctl login --output-token` (undocumented flag) will print the token string after verification on a machine that works, then you can set `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in WSL env.

jess: ok tried `--output-token` from mac, set REDWOOD_TOKEN in WSL and `redwoodctl profiles list` now shows the profile, yay. thanks. :tada:

michael: noted — we'll add clearer docs and a CLI flag that explicitly supports headless flows for WSL/CI. filed internal ticket DX-587.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for infra/redwoodctl v0.12.2 — contains auth retry fix (PR #2146). ETA 35m.

jess: perfect, that should remove the manual step. one more thing: when I copied config I noticed `current_profile: "default"` but redwoodctl still used `default` even though I created `work` profile. had to run `redwoodctl profiles set work` — maybe confusing for new users.

lisa: yep UX issue — config merging doesn't set current_profile on import. adding note to DX-588 to auto-select the first profile if none was set.

adam: small snippet that worked for me if folks need it: ```sh
mkdir -p ~/.redwood
cat > ~/.redwood/config.yaml <<'YAML'
profiles:
  work:
    token: "<paste-token>"
current_profile: work
YAML
```

jess: saved that. local serve now picks up the right profile and `redwoodctl local serve` runs. thanks everyone. :heart:

michael: follow-up: if anyone hits `invalid_verification_code` and the host clock is wrong, try `ntpdate` or update WSL clock; some providers check timestamps strictly.

lisa: will add a short troubleshooting blurb to the CLI quickstart doc (devex/cli.md).

jess: closing thread — workaround and doc help are sufficient for now. :white_check_mark:
